findings.issue: Wear and Favorites export used cached records, omitted another tab saves, and could claim a clean backup while current storage was corrupt or unreadable.
findings.repair: Fresh validated read on export. Readable invalid bytes are returned exactly for recovery; failed reads refuse stale backup. Favorites exposes refresh() for active UI/storage events.

findings.issue: A reviewed wear restore could erase unseen new events after the cached revision refreshed. Mutable/forged restore and Favorites previews were not bound to their original review.
findings.repair: Private preview identity, immutable payload binding and original raw/revision token checks. Wear consumes successful restore ticket; Favorites also validates no-op merges against backing bytes.

findings.issue: Favorites duplicate save could report already saved after a peer removed it; no-op imports could accept stale durable state.
findings.repair: Recheck exact backing bytes on duplicate add and no-op merge; refuse stale confirmation.

findings.issue: A verified successful save after a quota failure still reported memory-only status.
findings.repair: Restore persistent status after successful setItem and read-back verification.

findings.issue: Preference import rejected identical records solely because their JSON object property order differed.
findings.repair: Canonical duplicate comparison without replacing the saved record, changing its vote, or weakening true conflict checks.

findings.issue: A caller could edit a learning import preview after validation to change enabled state or erase/replace existing votes. Ordinary dialog held the object privately, but public store API accepted the mutated payload.
findings.repair: Private original-instance ticket binds copied current token and stable full preview payload; reject changes/clones/cross-instance use and consume after successful merge.

findings.status: fixed for active exclusive API; legacy synchronous compatibility limit remains documented
findings.issue: Whole-document localStorage compare/write is not atomic: two tabs could both report success while one saved Favorite/wear/learning record was lost.
findings.repair: Schema-preserving exclusive(callback) with namespace-specific native Web Locks and captured raw/revision check after queue wait. Persistent lockless saves refuse explicitly; memory-only operations queue locally. Root wraps active application writes.

findings.issue: Image-review export checked feedback before final awaited packet hashing; a newly rejected or changed outfit could then be published/downloaded. Initial feedback read failure also left busy latched.
findings.repair: Capture copied outfit/request/owner context/watch. Recheck after final async request, publish and actual download inside current-token guard, and always clear busy on read failure. Preserve frozen Standard panel and all image/source/import operations.

independent_cross_review_and_ui_run.note: Contains overlapping learning/lock tests plus another agent's actual UI preference and cross-review cases; do not add to final suite as a distinct-test count.

confirmed_no_new_defect: Independent rejection oracle and legacy/indexed tests cover canonical/wire selections, all eight scopes, occasion aliases/all historical Neither, static owner rules, overlapping Undo, temporary exclusions, mixed imports, concurrency and failed reads without altering original event payloads.
Overlapping tie-exposure append calls with distinct generation IDs preserve both successful immutable records; different namespaces are not read or rewritten.

Image-assessment store uses serialized IndexedDB readwrite transactions. Distinct batch inserts both persist; duplicate identical imports are idempotent; same-outfit conflict aborts without replacement; transaction abort preserves earlier batches and retry succeeds.

No approval/candidate metadata predicate in the audited persistence modules contradicts the approved five shirt appearance batches. No pixels, catalogue IDs, original source scoring tables or source-provenance metadata were modified by this agent.
boundaries_and_limits: Native Web Locks behavior is exercised here with a queue model; browser-level two-tab active UI verification is root-owned. Legacy synchronous mutation APIs and frozen old pages remain available for compatibility and do not acquire the new locks.

Rejection IndexedDB tests use fake-indexeddb; storage quota/native browser failure gates are verified separately by the parent. Same-revision out-of-band DB tampering is not claimed to be detected on every cached match.
Corrupt bytes are retained; invalid/unreadable stores block unsafe writes. This does not imply arbitrary corrupted ledgers are automatically repaired by an import.

Learning is intentionally occasion-scoped. Required-formality values remain recorded, but they do not create independent learned models. Root explicitly retained that numeric policy; characterization is in storage-learning-formality-characterization.json.

Image board rendering, underlying image content and live service behavior were not independently visually retested in this storage harness. The tested production guard/handler runs with stub image/network/DOM work and real rejection-store logic.
The canonical source catalogue regression passed; full shirt/collar provenance/visual inspection and protected-asset inventory are root-owned.
Archived variants listed here are distinguished from active entrypoint resources. No claim that all rollback snapshots or every archived module received a full independent review.
